agents.task:
Black-box reconnaissance and attack-surface mapping of https://cloudmate.onrender.com/ (the ONLY in-scope target — do not touch any other host/domain/IP).

Your job is recon ONLY, not vulnerability exploitation. Deliverables:
1. Technology fingerprint: server/framework headers, cookies, JS bundles, build tooling (e.g. React/Next/Vite), backend hints (Render.com hosting).
2. Full content map: crawl the site with katana/gospider (bounded depth, e.g. depth 3-4) plus a small ffuf/dirsearch pass for hidden paths (use a small wordlist like common.txt; keep request counts modest). Record every endpoint, path, form, and parameter found.
3. JS analysis: enumerate all loaded JS files, endpoints/API paths and secrets-looking strings inside them (note anything that looks like keys/tokens).
4. Auth model: identify login/signup flows, roles, session cookies, JWT usage, OAuth integrations. If there are test/demo accounts indicated, note them (do not create destructive changes; creating a throwaway account on the app is allowed if needed for mapping).
5. API surface: any /api/* endpoints, GraphQL, websockets.
6. Write findings to shared notes with create_note (category "wiki" for the target map, "general" for observations) so later agents can build on them. Record coverage entries (record_coverage) for surfaces you mapped.
7. After recon, call get_threat_model on https://cloudmate.onrender.com/ — if you observed enough to correct the baseline I'm about to write, use amend_threat_model.

Keep total requests bounded (a few hundred max). Report back via agent_finish with: technology stack, endpoint inventory, auth model, JS findings, and any suspicious surfaces worth deeper testing.

caveats: 1 agent(s) did not finish cleanly (Recon & Mapping Agent); any surface they held is under-covered.
